aurelia_auctioneer.name: Corin the Auctioneer
aurelia_auctioneer.description: An immaculate auctioneer whose warm smile never obscures the fact that every lot, bidder, and debt is being counted.

dialog.greeting: Aurelia does not ask where a remarkable thing came from. It asks whether you can prove it is yours to sell.
dialog.trade: Bring rare materials, not tall tales. The hall has heard both.

aurelia_auctioneer.default_dialog: Corin studies a valuation slip before returning your attention.

aurelia_archivist.name: Elion the Archivist
aurelia_archivist.description: A meticulous city archivist with ink-stained cuffs and the wary impatience of someone whose records keep proving that old problems are not finished problems.

dialog.greeting: The city has records for every road, ruin, and observatory. What it lacks are current observations from people willing to go there.
dialog.observatory: The hill observatory is not abandoned in the historical sense. It is abandoned in the dangerous sense.

aurelia_archivist.default_dialog: Elion holds a page to the light, checking the watermark before speaking.

aurelia_surveyor.name: Lyra the Surveyor
aurelia_surveyor.description: A field surveyor with sun-bleached sleeves, a brass compass, and a stack of route reports that seem to multiply whenever she looks away.

dialog.greeting: A road does not become safe because someone drew it in ink. It becomes safe when someone comes back with measurements.
dialog.survey: The outlands change faster than city maps admit.

aurelia_surveyor.default_dialog: Lyra checks a compass bearing against the margin of a field map.

aurelia_artificer.name: Ves the Artificer
aurelia_artificer.description: A practical master artificer whose scarred gloves and exacting eye make even a simple tool inspection feel like an examination.

dialog.greeting: Good work survives the road. Good tools help it get there.
dialog.trade: I carry tools and sound gear. The rare work, you will have to earn.

aurelia_artificer.default_dialog: Ves tests the balance of a hammer before setting it back on the rack.
